# 3. Model Trainnig and Tuning (Validation)

# 5. Item Correct Rate of Sub-population

$$P(Y) = \Sigma_{\theta}   P(Y=1|\theta)*P(\theta)$$

## 5-1. Cut point and SEM

$$ \theta_{sub} = (cutpoint - 1SEM, cutpoint + 1SEM) $$

1.  Use only test type A and G excluding type B having 15 items.
2.  Calculate item information
3.  Test information = sum(item information)
4.  CSEM\^2 = 1/Test information
5.  Take the average of all squared CSEMs across test types.
6.  Take the square root of the previous stage
7.  Cut point = -1.4
8.  Specify the range of theta for sub-population around the cut point

## 5-2. Weight for sub-population

$$ P(\theta_{sub})$$

-   Find the pnorm of theta points using pnorm(mean = 0, sd = 1)
-   Calculate weight using the summation of the all pnorm as denominator

# 6. Predicting item difficulty with Explanatory IRT and Machine Learning

## 6-1. Explanatory IRT Process (Bayesian/Maximum Liklihood)

1.  Split the response data into train and test sets (person x item)
2.  Fit explanatory 2PL IRT using train data
3.  Predict the response data of test set using the parameter estimates 
$$ Y \sim  Bernoulli(inv\_logit(\theta + (\mu + \Sigma_{m} \beta_{m}X_im + e))) $$
4.  Calculate the classical based-correct rate

### 6-1-1. Bayesian

- Software: stan
- Model: Rasch, 2PL

### 6-1-2. Maximum Likelihood 

- Software: lme4::glmer
- Model: Rasch


## 6-2. Machine learning Process

1.  Calculate the classical-based correct rate based on the item X covariate matrix file
2.  Split the data into train and test sets (item x covariate)
3.  Fit machine learning model using train data
4.  Predict the classical based-correct rate of test set
